messages:
elena_support: customer reporting spikes of 403s on /v1/embeddings since ~2026-03-05 14:10 UTC. They see request_id headers: req_4f2a9c and req_4f2aac. Customer says this started after rotating a proj-scoped svc key.

customer_acctrep: hey, we rotated our service key and then started getting 403s for some old clients. repro curl attached below — works for some projects but not others.

julian_eng: can you paste the exact curl you used? also include the X-Org and X-Project headers you sent. 403 could be scope mismatch or canonicalization issue.

customer_acctrep: sure — here's the curl they used (redacted token):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: org-acme" \
  -H "X-Project-Id: proj-42/" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

elena_support: note the trailing slash on X-Project-Id — we've seen header canonicalization cause signed-header mismatches before. can you try without trailing slash and capture the failing request_id?

customer_acctrep: tried no-trailing-slash, still intermittent. new req: req_8b9c01.

matthew_sre: pulled auth logs for those req ids. relevant lines: 
```
[2026-03-05T14:11:02Z] req=req_4f2a9c auth=svckey-proj42 provided_sig=Z1y7... computed_sig=Z1y7... status=200
[2026-03-05T14:12:18Z] req=req_4f2aac auth=svckey-proj42 provided_sig=Qv3k... computed_sig=Qv3k_mismatch status=403 reason=signature_mismatch
[2026-03-05T14:20:11Z] req=req_8b9c01 auth=svckey-proj42 provided_sig=Am5r... computed_sig=Am5r_mismatch status=403 reason=header_order
```

julian_eng: header_order as reason — that means the signing client and our verifier are sorting headers differently. Do you have the signed headers list in the auth header? e.g. `SignedHeaders=host;content-type;x-org-id;x-project-id`

customer_acctrep: yes, their auth header includes `SignedHeaders=host;content-type;x-project-id;x-org-id` (project before org). looks like ordering mismatch.

elena_support: aha. their client signs headers in insertion order; our verifier normalizes to alphabetical. most clients are okay because canonicalization happens client-side, but this svc key was generated by a library that preserves insertion order.

matthew_sre: short-term: ask customer to re-order SignedHeaders alphabetically when building signature. Can also repro by constructing a curl with manually set `Authorization: Signature ... SignedHeaders=...`

julian_eng: longer term we should accept any header order. filing infra issue to normalize on verifier side. ops_lead, can we schedule a small fix?

ops_lead: yes, creating ticket INFRA-2319. patch will normalize header parsing and recompute sigs on incoming requests before strict comparison. low-risk change, target next patch window. :thumbsup:

elena_support: for immediate repro/debug bundle — please ask customer to collect:
- the curl they used (full headers)
- output of `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac <key> -binary | base64` for their signature step (or equivalent)
- the full raw request captured with tcpdump or curl --trace-ascii to include exact header ordering
- the request ids (req_4f2a9c, req_4f2aac, req_8b9c01)

customer_acctrep: i'll get those and share a debug bundle. also FYI there was a low-risk deploy around the time they saw the first 403 — deploy-bot posted:

deploy-bot: deployed infra/verify-normalization @ commit abc123 at 2026-03-05T14:09:45Z

julian_eng: that deploy touched the auth verifier only in staging, not prod — but good to note. matthew, can you confirm there were no concurrent cache invalidates or key rotations around 14:10?

matthew_sre: checked rotation logs: svckey for proj-42 rotated at 2026-03-04T09:00Z earlier, no rotations during the 14:10 window. no cache flushes either.

elena_support: next steps for customer: re-run the failing curl with `--trace-ascii trace.txt`, capture the raw trace, and upload it along with the HMAC step output. we'll attach to INFRA-2319 and keep this thread updated.

customer_acctrep: uploading bundle now, will post link when ready. thanks all! :pray:

julian_eng: thanks — once we have the trace we can reproduce locally by replaying the raw request (using nc or --http1.1 with --resolve) and confirm verifier change fixes it.

matthew_sre: marking this one as customer-impacting but limited. will watch for new req ids after their bundle.

elena_support: closing loop here when INFRA-2319 is merged.
